dedupe_keys.name: dg qram quantitative risk assessment model for dangerous goods transport through road tunnels piarc oecd

description: DG-QRAM (Dangerous Goods Quantitative Risk Assessment Model) evaluates the risks of transporting dangerous goods through road tunnels and along alternative routes. It was developed jointly by the World Road Association (PIARC) and the OECD in the ERS2 project (1997-2001) and PIARC sells and updates it. The PIARC page says it assesses the societal risk of a tunnel or route, compares it with reference criteria, and assesses the risk for each ADR tunnel category (A to E) to help choose one; it can serve the specific risk analysis within the general risk analysis required by European Directive 2004/54/EC on tunnel safety. Coverage: 13 incident scenarios representing key dangerous goods groups, from a heavy goods vehicle fire without dangerous goods (20 MW) to BLEVEs and vapour cloud explosions of LPG and motor spirit and releases of chlorine, ammonia and acrolein; it accounts for accident frequencies from historical data, physical consequences in tunnels and on open routes, escape and shelter, and the effects of heat and smoke on people. Format and access: Microsoft Excel based software, version 4.10, ordered from PIARC. Inputs cover route sections, tunnel geometry, ventilation, drainage, emergency exits, traffic mix and speeds, dangerous goods volumes, incident rates and population along the route. Cost: EUR 2,500 for a new licence and EUR 1,000 or 2,000 for updates. Licence: proprietary, with conditions of use that were not read. Caveats: the page warns that its algorithms date from 1998 and that smoke propagation and evacuation need other tools. Simulation uses: societal risk (F-N curves) for tunnel routing and hazardous materials policy. Related records: HDM-4 (model-hdm-4-highway-development-and-management) is the other PIARC road tool.
